mainTopic: Kosher סכך layouts: boards with פסולת, narrowing air gaps and לבוד in the middle, a broken house roof, a fish digression, and roofing an אכסדרה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: even רבי מאיר agrees that boards spaced one board-width apart, with kosher פסולת in the gaps, make a כשרה סוכה. The גמרא asks how this works for the view that 4 טפחים of סכך פסול in the middle disqualifies. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers with a סוכה exactly 8 אמות wide, roofed from both walls so that kosher פסולת meets in the center. Next, אביי rules on narrowing a three-טפחים air gap, which works differently in a large סוכה and a small one. רב אחא and רבינא then argue whether לבוד works in the middle of the roof, and the גמרא pushes aside the proof brought for each side. רבי יהודה בר אלעאי teaches two broad rulings, a broken house roof covered with סכך and the אברומא fish, and each one is narrowed when explained. A side discussion explains why אביי permitted the small fish of the בב River, and רבינא says they are forbidden today. Finally, אביי and רבא argue about roofing an אכסדרה without פצימין, and the explanation of אביי's view continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees when the gaps equal the boards
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that רבי מאיר agrees a סוכה made of boards is כשרה if each gap is as wide as a board and is filled with kosher פסולת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר agrees that if the space between one board and the next is the full width of a board, a person puts kosher פסולת between them, and the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its statement about roofing with wide boards. It says that even רבי מאיר, who is strict about boards, agrees to one case where the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a board 4 טפחים wide is סכך פסול. Here he agrees that if the boards are spaced one board-width apart and the gaps are filled with kosher פסולת, the סוכה is כשרה. The ברייתא does not say why. That missing reason is what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (concedes): an opinion that is usually strict admits to one case
A board (here, one about 4 טפחים wide)
The full width of a board
Leftover material from the threshing floor or winepress. It is kosher סכך.

steps.confusionAlert: Here פְּסָל means kosher leftover material (פסולת), which is good סכך. It does NOT mean 'פסול' (invalid). Do not mix up these two similar-looking words.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir concedes
that if there is, between one board and another board,
a gap the full width of a board,
then one places waste (kosher leftover material) between them
and the sukkah is fit.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא does not explain why. The גמרא will question this in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about roofing with boards 4 טפחים wide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי מאיר, boards spaced one board-width apart, with kosher פסולת filling the gaps, make a כשרה סוכה.

steps.title: Why is it kosher according to the 4-handbreadth view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: this ruling makes sense for the view that סכך פסול disqualifies only at 4 אמות, but not for the view that 4 טפחים in the middle disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says that סכך פסול, whether in the middle or on the side, disqualifies only at 4 אמות. That is why this סוכה is כשרה. But according to the one who says that in the middle it disqualifies at 4 טפחים, why is it כשרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling. It works fine under one opinion but seems impossible under another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two views about how much סכך פסול ruins a סוכה. If the amount is 4 אמות everywhere, then one 4-טפחים board is far too small to matter. But if just 4 טפחים in the middle is enough, then every single board in the middle should already ruin the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this view works, but that view doesn't' question)
According to the one who says
In the middle of the סוכה
On the side, next to the wall

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the units. 'אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת' means 4 cubits (about 24 טפחים). 'אַרְבָּעָה' alone means 4 טפחים (handbreadths). The whole question depends on this difference.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
that both in the middle and on the side
unfit roofing disqualifies only with four cubits,
that is why it is fit (no board is four cubits wide).
But according to the one who says
that in the middle it disqualifies with four handbreadths,
why is it fit?
phrases.notes: Each board is already 4 טפחים, which should be enough to disqualify the סוכה in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע בֵּין מִן הַצַּד בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי מאיר's concession in Step 1 using the view that 4 טפחים of סכך פסול in the middle disqualifies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the board-and-פסולת סוכה is כשרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the view that 4 טפחים of סכך פסול in the middle disqualifies, each 4-טפחים board in the middle should disqualify the סוכה.

steps.title: A סוכה of exactly eight cubits roofed from both sides
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the case is a סוכה exactly 8 אמות wide, roofed from each wall with three boards, each followed by a strip of פסולת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: Here we are dealing with a סוכה that is exactly 8 אמות wide. He places a board, then פסולת, a board, then פסולת, a board, then פסולת, starting from this side. Then he does the same from the other side: a board, then פסולת, three times.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the question by limiting the ברייתא to one specific layout. He describes exactly how the roof is arranged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 8 אמות equals 48 טפחים. From each wall there are 3 boards and 3 strips of פסולת, each 4 טפחים wide, for a total of 24 טפחים per side. Because each side begins with a board at the wall and ends with פסולת, the two last פסולת strips meet in the exact center. The next step spells out what that achieves.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with (a specific case): a formula that narrows the case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Here, with a sukkah that is no more than
exactly eight cubits, we are dealing,
and he places a board and waste,
and a board and waste, and a board and waste,
from this side,
and a board and waste, and a board and waste,
and a board and waste, from that side,
phrases.notes: Another 24 טפחים from the second wall. Total: 48 טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָכָא בְּסוּכָּה דְּלָא הָוְיָא אֶלָּא שְׁמֹנֶה מְצוּמְצָמוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2 by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא speaks only of a specific size and layout.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ברייתא meant any סוכה with boards and פסולת. Then the boards in the middle would disqualify it under the 4-טפחים view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a סוכה exactly 8 אמות wide, roofed symmetrically from both walls, so that no board lands in the center.

steps.title: Kosher roofing ends up in the center
steps.stepSummary: With this layout, two strips of פסולת meet in the middle, giving a kosher center to the סוכה. Therefore it is כשרה even under the 4-טפחים view.
steps.simpleTranslation: So there end up being two strips of פסולת in the middle, and there is enough for a kosher סוכה in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב הונא's answer by showing the result of the layout: the center of the סוכה is kosher roofing, not a board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two 4-טפחים strips of פסולת meet to form 8 טפחים of kosher סכך in the center. That is more than the 7 טפחים minimum for a סוכה. No board sits in the middle, so the 4-טפחים rule never applies. Each side's boards are within 20 טפחים of the wall, which is less than 4 אמות, so they are treated as part of the wall through דופן עקומה. The סוכה is therefore כשרה under both views.

keyTerms.meaning: So that there are / it turns out that there are
Two strips of kosher leftover material
The minimum size needed for a valid סוכה (7×7 טפחים)

steps.whatToRemember: Under the view that 4 טפחים of סכך פסול in the middle disqualifies, רבי מאיר's concession works only in a precise case. The סוכה is exactly 8 אמות wide, and three boards with פסולת are laid from each wall. This leaves 8 טפחים of kosher פסולת in the center. The boards on each side are less than 4 אמות from the wall, so they count as a bent wall (דופן עקומה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the two rules work together. The 4-טפחים rule protects the middle of the סוכה, while the 4-אמות rule and דופן עקומה deal with the sides. A careful layout can satisfy both.

phrases.english: so that there are two strips of waste in the middle,
phrases.notes: 4 + 4 = 8 טפחים of kosher סכך in the center.

phrases.english: and there is the measure of a fit sukkah in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's answer from Step 3 by stating the result of the layout.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סוכה is כשרה because the center has 8 טפחים of kosher פסולת (more than the minimum for a סוכה). The boards on each side are less than 4 אמות from the wall, so they are covered by דופן עקומה.

steps.title: Narrowing a three-handbreadth air gap in a large or small sukkah
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that narrowing a three-טפחים air gap always works in a large סוכה. In a small סוכה it works only if the gap is narrowed with kosher material like reeds, not with metal skewers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if there is an open gap of three טפחים in a large סוכה and someone narrowed it, it counts as narrowed whether he used reeds or skewers. In a small סוכה, narrowing with reeds counts. Narrowing with skewers does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. אביי gives a ruling about fixing an air gap of three טפחים in the סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An air gap of three טפחים is too big for לבוד, so the סכך on its two sides is not joined. Once the gap is narrowed below three, לבוד can close it. In a large סוכה, even unfit material like skewers is acceptable, because a small strip of פסול material does not disqualify. In a small סוכה (just 7×7 טפחים), the area under the skewers does not count as kosher סוכה space, so not enough kosher space is left.

keyTerms.meaning: Open air: a gap with no covering in the סכך
Narrowing or reducing (here, making the gap smaller)
Reeds, which are kosher סכך material
Metal skewers or spits, which are not kosher as סכך
A small סוכה, only the minimum size of 7×7 טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the skewers is NOT that they are wide enough to disqualify the סוכה, since three טפחים of סכך פסול is not enough to disqualify. In a small סוכה, the problem is that the space under them does not count toward the minimum kosher size.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
An open gap of three handbreadths in a large sukkah, and one narrowed it,
whether with reeds or with skewers,
phrases.notes: Reeds are kosher roofing; skewers are not.

phrases.english: it counts as a valid narrowing.
In a small sukkah, with reeds, it counts as a narrowing;
with skewers, it does not count as a narrowing.
phrases.notes: The area under the skewers does not count toward the minimum 7×7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲוִיר שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּסוּכָּה גְּדוֹלָה וּמִיעֲטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the board-and-פסולת discussion closed in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrowing a three-טפחים gap always works in a large סוכה. In a small סוכה it works only with kosher material.

steps.title: Side gap versus middle gap: does לבוד work in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits אביי's rule to a gap at the side of the סוכה. For a gap in the middle, רב אחא and רבינא disagree on whether לבוד applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only at the side. But in the middle, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says לבוד works in the middle. The other says לבוד does not work in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows אביי's ruling to a gap near the wall. It then reports a מחלוקת about a gap in the middle of the סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the side, the small leftover gap can be treated as closed against the wall. In the middle, the question is whether two separate sections of סכך can be joined across a small gap. One אמורא says yes; the other says לבוד only works at the side.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only (introduces a limitation)
Treating a gap of less than three טפחים as if it were closed
At the side, near the wall

phrases.english: And this applies only at the side.
But in the middle,
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
One said: there is lavud in the middle,
and one said: there is no lavud in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי מִן הַצַּד. אֲבָל בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's rule to a side gap and opens a מחלוקת about a middle gap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's rule is certain only at the side. Whether לבוד applies in the middle is disputed.

steps.title: What is the reason of the view that לבוד works in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source or reasoning behind the view that לבוד applies in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who said לבוד works in the middle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what supports the lenient view, so that it can bring a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more surprising claim is that לבוד can join two pieces in the middle, with no wall involved. So the גמרא wants to know where that idea comes from.

phrases.english: What is the reason
of the one who said there is lavud in the middle?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ לָבוּד בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of one side of the מחלוקת in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for applying לבוד in the middle.

steps.title: Support from a ברייתא about alleyway beams
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a קורה used for an alley (מבוי). Two beams sticking out from opposite walls count as joined if the gap between them is less than three טפחים. That is לבוד in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a beam sticks out from one wall and does not touch the other wall. Or two beams stick out, one from each wall, and they do not touch each other. If the gap is less than three, you do not need another beam. If it is three, you need another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. It shows a case where לבוד joins two pieces across a gap in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-beam case, the gap is between the two beams, out in the middle, not against a wall. Still, if the gap is under three טפחים, the beams count as one continuous beam. So the ברייתא seems to prove that לבוד applies in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: A crossbeam placed over an alley's entrance to allow carrying there on שבת
Less than three טפחים, the measure for לבוד

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main textual support for applying לבוד in the middle. It is a useful precedent beyond סוכה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
A beam that projects from this wall
and does not touch the other wall,
and similarly two beams,
one projecting from this wall
and one projecting from the other wall
and they do not touch each other:

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: If less than three, one need not bring another beam.
If three, one must bring another beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא of two beams joined by לבוד across a middle gap.
steps.raayaObject: The view that יש לבוד באמצע

steps.title: The other view: beams are only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The view that rejects לבוד in the middle answers that alley beams are different. Their whole system is דרבנן, so the חכמים could be lenient there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? He says beams are different, because they are only a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the second opinion handles the ברייתא. The leniency for beams cannot be applied to סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on carrying in an alley, and the beam that fixes it, are rabbinic rules. Since the rules are only דרבנן, the חכמים allowed לבוד even in the middle there. That does not prove the same for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other opinion, how does he answer?

steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about לבוד in the middle. The beam ברייתא supports the lenient side. The other side answers that beams are only דרבנן and prove nothing about other laws.

phrases.english: And the other (Sage)?
Beams are different, as they are rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes aside the proof from step 8 on behalf of the stricter view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the beam ברייתא as proof for לבוד in the middle in other areas of law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The beam case is rabbinic, so leniency there cannot be carried over to other laws such as סוכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת stands. The beam ברייתא does not settle it.

steps.title: What is the source for the view that rejects לבוד in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: After proving the other side earlier, the גמרא now asks for the reasoning of the view that לבוד does not apply in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who said that לבוד does not apply in the middle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second opinion and asks for its source. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7–8 gave a source for the view that לבוד DOES apply in the middle (the alley beams). Now the גמרא balances the discussion by asking what supports the opposite view.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said (refers to one side of a dispute)
Middle (a gap in the middle of the roof, not at the side)

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who said
there is no לבוד in the middle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 7, now asking for the opposite view's source after Step 9 defended that view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning for the view that לבוד does not apply in the middle.

steps.title: Proof from a skylight in a house's roof
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about a skylight in a roof treats a small hole as truly open for טומאה, which suggests no לבוד in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Suppose a house has a skylight with an opening of one טפח. If there is טומאה in the house, the whole house is טמא, but whatever is right under the skylight is טהור. If the טומאה is right under the skylight, the whole house is טהור. Suppose the skylight does not have an opening of one טפח. If there is טומאה in the house, whatever is under the skylight is טהור. If the טומאה is under the skylight, the whole house is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a משנה about טומאת אוהל. A skylight hole in the middle of a roof is treated as a real opening, even though it is smaller than three טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לבוד applied in the middle, a hole smaller than three טפחים would count as closed. Then the roof would cover everything, and the spot under the skylight would become טמא too. Since the משנה says the spot under the skylight stays טהור, the hole is not closed by לבוד. This shows that לבוד does not apply in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: Skylight, an opening in the roof
An opening of one square טפח, the minimum size that counts for טומאת אוהל
Ritual impurity (here, from a dead body spreading under a roof)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about whether the hole is one טפח or smaller. The point is that in every case, a hole smaller than three טפחים is NOT treated as closed. If לבוד worked in the middle, it would be closed.

phrases.english: As we learned: a skylight in a house
and it has an opening of one טפח,
if the impurity is in the house, all of it is impure,
but what is opposite the skylight is pure.
If the impurity is opposite the skylight,
the entire house is pure.
If the skylight does not have an opening of a טפח,
if the impurity is in the house, what is opposite the skylight is pure.
If the impurity is opposite the skylight,
the entire house is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The skylight משנה treats a hole of less than three טפחים in the middle of a roof as open, so לבוד does not apply in the middle.

steps.title: Laws of טומאה are a special tradition
steps.stepSummary: The view that accepts לבוד in the middle answers that הלכות טומאה are a received tradition and cannot teach about other areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? Laws of טומאה are different, because that is how they were received by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other opinion handles the skylight proof. It answers that טומאה laws are a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of אהלות were passed down as הלכה למשה מסיני, with their own exact details. So the fact that לבוד does not close a skylight for טומאה does not prove anything about סוכה. The proof is pushed aside, and the dispute stays open. This mirrors Step 9, where the alley proof was pushed aside as דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other (opinion)? How does he answer?
They learned by tradition (received from סיני)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs were rejected. Alley beams are דרבנן, and טומאה laws are a received tradition. Neither area can decide whether לבוד applies in the middle for סוכה.

phrases.english: And the other opinion?
The laws of impurity are different,
for that is how they learned them by tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the skylight, not the view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Laws of טומאה are a unique tradition, so you cannot learn other areas of law from them.

steps.title: A house with a broken roof covered with סכך
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי teaches that if a house's roof breaks open and one puts סכך over the hole, it is a kosher סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי taught: A house whose roof broke open, where someone put סכך over the hole, is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. A house roof has a hole, the hole is filled with סכך, and רבי יהודה בר אלעאי says it is a kosher סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the leftover house roof around the hole is not kosher סכך. The ruling as stated sounds like it is always kosher, with no limit. That is why it is about to be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Was broken open (a hole in the roof)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai taught:
A house that was broken open (in its roof)
and one put סכך over it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the לבוד discussion closes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house with a broken roof, with סכך placed over the hole, is a kosher סוכה.

steps.title: Request to explain the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asks רבי יהודה to spell out the ruling more precisely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said before him: רבי, explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks for the ruling to be made more precise. This sets up the clarification that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling 'kosher' sounds unlimited, but the leftover roof is פסול material. The request asks under what conditions the סוכה is actually kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: He said before him (respectfully, to a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
My teacher, explain it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: רַבִּי, פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limits of the ruling in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact conditions under which the broken-roof סוכה is kosher.

steps.title: Four אמות of leftover roof is the limit
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is clarified: if the leftover roof between the wall and the hole is four אמות, the סוכה is פסולה; if less, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is how Father explained it: four אמות is פסולה; less than four אמות is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling gets its limit. It depends on how wide the leftover house roof is between the wall and the סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leftover roof is less than four אמות, we view it as if the wall bends over and continues along the top. This idea is called דופן עקומה, and it lets the סכך sit right next to the 'wall.' If the leftover roof is four אמות or more, the wall cannot be seen as bending that far, so the סוכה is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Father (the speaker's father, cited as the source of the explanation)
Four cubits, the limit for פסול roofing next to the wall
A 'bent wall': פסול roofing treated as part of the wall bending over

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase כך פירש אבא is read in two ways. Some read it as רבי יהודה answering in the name of his own father. Others read it as רבי ישמעאל citing his father, רבי יוסי. Either way, the content of the rule is the same.
steps.whatToRemember: A broken house roof with סכך over the hole is kosher only if the leftover roof is less than four אמות wide.
steps.whyThisMatters: This applies the principle of דופן עקומה, already taught in the משנה, to a house with a broken roof. It is a key principle for kosher סוכות built under partial roofs.

phrases.english: This is how Father explained it:
four אמות, it is unfit;
less than four אמות, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request of Step 14 by limiting the ruling of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leftover roof of four אמות makes the סוכה פסולה; less than four אמות makes it כשרה.

steps.title: The small fish called אברומא is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי teaches that the small fish אברומא may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי taught: the אברומא fish is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי, this time about a small fish. It is quoted here because, just like his סוכה ruling, it also needed clarification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אברומא is a tiny fish that is usually caught in nets together with other small fish, some of which may be non-kosher. Stated broadly, the ruling sounds like a blanket permission to eat it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The pattern repeats: a broad ruling from רבי יהודה בר אלעאי is followed by a request to define it more precisely.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai taught:
The avroma fish is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching by the same תנא, brought because it follows the same pattern of being clarified by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אברומא fish is permitted to eat.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל asks for a precise explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asks רבי יהודה to explain the fish ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said before him: רבי, explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asks for the ruling to be spelled out. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not disagreeing. He is asking for the boundaries of the ruling, because a blanket permission could be misunderstood.

keyTerms.meaning: Said before him (respectfully, to a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
My teacher, explain it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the ruling in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In exactly which cases is the אברומא permitted?

steps.title: It depends on the location
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is clarified: in one place the fish is forbidden, and in another it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what my father said: the fish of such-and-such a place is forbidden, and the fish of such-and-such a place is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that the permission is not universal. It depends on where the fish comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where non-kosher fish live in the same waters, they may get mixed in with the אברומא, so it is forbidden. Where no non-kosher fish are found, it is permitted. The broad ruling was really a location-based ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The אברומא is permitted only in waters where non-kosher fish are not found.

phrases.english: This is what my father said:
The fish of such-and-such a place is forbidden,
the fish of such-and-such a place is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for clarification in step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission depends on the location: forbidden where non-kosher fish are present, permitted where they are not.

steps.title: אביי permits the small fish of the בב River
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares this to אביי's ruling that the small fish of the בב River are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what אביי said: these small fish of the בב River are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar location-based ruling from אביי. Small fish from one specific river are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the אברומא, אביי's permission depends on the place. This raises a question: what is special about this river?

phrases.english: Like that which Abaye said:
These small fish of the Bav River are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case showing the same idea: permission based on location
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The small fish of the בב River are permitted.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי permitted these fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling. This sets up a series of proposed answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know what natural feature of this river keeps non-kosher fish out.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are non-kosher fish not a concern in the בב River?

steps.title: First suggestion: the current is too strong
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the water flows so fast that non-kosher fish, which lack a spinal cord, cannot survive there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the water flows fast, and a non-kosher fish, since it has no spinal cord, cannot stay there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a first reason: the strong current sweeps non-kosher fish away. The word אילימא signals that this suggestion is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that non-kosher fish are physically weaker. Without a spinal cord they cannot hold their place in a rushing river, so only kosher fish would remain.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that is usually rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is because the water flows fast,
and a non-kosher fish,
since it has no spinal cord,
cannot stay there —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rapid current drives out non-kosher fish because they lack a spinal cord.

steps.title: Objection: we see them survive in fast water
steps.stepSummary: Experience shows that non-kosher fish do live in fast-flowing rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that they do stay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion based on what people actually observe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-kosher fish are seen living in rivers with strong currents. So the current cannot be what keeps them out of the בב River.

keyTerms.meaning: But we see (rejection based on observation)

phrases.english: But we see that they do stay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 21
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts observation: non-kosher fish do survive in strong currents.

steps.title: Second suggestion: the water is too salty
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the water is salty, and non-kosher fish, which lack scales, cannot survive in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because the water is salty, and a non-kosher fish, since it has no scales, cannot stay there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second reason: salt water drives away fish that have no scales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scales are a sign of a kosher fish. The suggestion is that without scales to protect them, non-kosher fish cannot live in salty water.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the water is salty,
and a non-kosher fish,
since it has no scales,
cannot stay there —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 21 with a new one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The salty water drives out non-kosher fish because they lack scales.

steps.title: Objection: we see them survive in salt water
steps.stepSummary: Experience shows that non-kosher fish do live in salty water.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that they do stay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion with the same kind of observation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-kosher fish are seen living in salt water, so saltiness cannot explain why the בב River is free of them.

phrases.english: But we see that they do stay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 23
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts observation: non-kosher fish do survive in salt water.

steps.title: The real reason: the mud does not let them breed
steps.stepSummary: The mud of this river does not allow non-kosher fish to reproduce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because their mud does not let non-kosher fish multiply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the riverbed itself does not support non-kosher fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether non-kosher fish can survive in the water. It is that they cannot reproduce in this river's mud, so they are not found there.
steps.whatToRemember: The בב River's small fish are permitted because its mud does not allow non-kosher fish to breed.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it does not let multiply,
their mud, non-kosher fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מְרַבֵּה טִינַיְיהוּ דָּג טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final accepted answer after two rejections
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Non-kosher fish cannot reproduce in the mud of the בב River, so its small fish are permitted.

steps.title: רבינא: today the fish are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Now that other rivers flow into the בב, its small fish are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: and nowadays, since נהר איתן and נהר גמדא pour into there, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא updates אביי's ruling. Conditions have changed, so the ruling has changed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other rivers now feed into the בב and can carry non-kosher fish in from outside. Even if they do not breed there, they may be present, so the fish may not be eaten without checking.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling based on natural conditions changes when those conditions change.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
And nowadays, since the Eitan River pours
and the Gamda River into there, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the conclusion of step 25 to earlier times
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Today, since other rivers flow into the בב, its small fish are forbidden without inspection.

steps.title: Dispute about roofing a portico without posts
steps.stepSummary: Roofing an אכסדרה with פצימין is kosher. Without פצימין, אביי says kosher and רבא says פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if one put סכך over a portico that has posts, it is kosher. If it has no posts, אביי said it is kosher, and רבא said it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to סוכה and introduces a new dispute between אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה is a roofed porch whose fourth side is open. When there are posts on the open side, everyone agrees the סוכה is kosher. The argument is only about a porch without posts.

keyTerms.meaning: Portico, a porch open on one side
Posts or doorposts on the open side

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the dispute covers every אכסדרה. With פצימין, both agree it is kosher. They argue only when there are no פצימין.

phrases.english: It was stated: if one put schach over a portico
that has posts, it is kosher.
If it has no posts,
Abaye said: it is kosher,
and Rava said: it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fish digression and opens a new סוכה dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אכסדרה with פצימין is kosher. Without פצימין, אביי rules it kosher and רבא rules it unfit.

steps.title: Starting to explain אביי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why אביי rules the סוכה kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said it is kosher —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא repeats אביי's opinion so it can explain his reasoning, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is repeated on purpose, as the opening of an explanation. The actual reason comes right on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Abaye said it is kosher —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates אביי's view to introduce his reasoning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the explanation of אביי's ruling that the סוכה is kosher.
